title.en: Volume 399 Biographies 158: Zheng Jue, Wang Tingxiu, Chou Yu, Gao Deng, Lou Yinliang, Song Ruwei
title.raw: 卷三百九十九 列傳第一百五十八 鄭瑴 王庭秀 仇悆 高登 婁寅亮 宋汝爲 Volume 399 Biographies 158: Zheng Jue, Wang Tingxiu, Chou Yu, Gao Deng, Lou Yinliang, Song Ruwei

sentences.zh: 鄭𣪝

translations.literal: Zheng Jue
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue

sentences.zh: 鄭𣪝，字致剛，建州人。

translations.literal: Zheng Jue, courtesy name Zhigang, was a native of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue, whose courtesy name was Zhigang, came from Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 政和八年舉進士，授安陸府教授，權信陽縣尉，監南康酒稅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenghe he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Professor of Anlu Prefecture, acting Magistrate of Xinyang County, and Supervisor of the wine tax at Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1118 he earned his jinshi degree and held successive posts as professor in Anlu Prefecture, acting magistrate of Xinyang County, and overseer of the wine tax at Nankang.

sentences.zh: 遂召為御史臺主簿。

translations.literal: He was then summoned to serve as Registrar of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the Censorate as registrar.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌之僭號也，挺身見高宗於濟州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne, he went forth boldly to meet Emperor Gaozong at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang seized the throne, he went in person to present himself to the future Emperor Gaozong at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 既即位，擢監察御史，遷右司諫，升為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After Gaozong took the throne, he was promoted to Investigating Censor, transferred to Right Remonstrance Officer, and advanced to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozong had ascended the throne, Zheng was promoted to investigating censor, then right remonstrance officer, and finally remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 帝至杭州，𣪝奏曰：「陛下南渡出於倉卒，省臺寺監、百司之臣獲濟者鮮，當擢吳中之秀以為用。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Hangzhou, Jue memorialized: "Your Majesty's southward crossing was made in haste; few ministers of the ministries, directorates, and various offices escaped safely—talented men of the Wu region should be promoted for service.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Hangzhou, Zheng Jue submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty's flight south was hurried, and few officials from the central ministries and bureaus made it through safely. You should promote outstanding men from the Wu region to serve the court.

sentences.zh: 況天下賢俊多避地吳、越，宜令守臣體訪境內寄居待闕，及見任宮觀等京朝官以上，各具姓名以聞，簡拔任使，庶幾速得賢才以濟艱厄。」

translations.literal: Moreover, many worthy men throughout the realm have taken refuge in Wu and Yue; local officials should be ordered to inquire within their jurisdictions into those residing there awaiting appointment, as well as capital officials currently serving in palace posts and the like, each reporting names so that the worthy may be selected and appointed, thereby quickly obtaining talent to meet this crisis."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, many talented men have fled to Wu and Yue. Local officials should be instructed to seek out within their jurisdictions those living there while awaiting appointment, as well as capital officials currently holding palace sinecures, report their names, and select the best for office—so that worthy men may be found quickly to meet the present emergency."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 苗傅、劉正彥等逆亂，𣪝庭立面折二凶，且謂逆賊凶焰熾甚，非請外援無可為者。

translations.literal: When Miao Fu, Liu Zhengyan, and others rebelled, Jue confronted the two villains face to face in court and said the rebels' ferocity was extreme and nothing could be done without requesting outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rose in rebellion, Zheng Jue stood in court and rebuked the two ringleaders to their faces, declaring that the rebels' power was too great and that outside help would be indispensable.

sentences.zh: 乃上章待罪求去，退見呂頤浩，議興復計，太后降詔不允。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial accepting blame and requesting dismissal, withdrew to meet Lü Yihao and discuss plans for restoration, and the Empress Dowager issued an edict refusing his request.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial accepting blame and asking to resign, withdrew to confer with Lü Yihao on plans to restore the throne, and the empress dowager issued an edict refusing to let him go.

sentences.zh: 朱勝非言𣪝面折二凶事，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei reported Jue's face-to-face rebuke of the two villains, and he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei reported how Zheng Jue had confronted the two rebels in court, and Zheng was appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時二凶竊威福之柄，肆行殺戮，日至都堂侵紊機政。

translations.literal: At that time the two villains usurped the power to grant favor and punishment, carried out killings at will, and daily came to the chief council chamber to interfere with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the two rebels had seized control of rewards and punishments, slaughtered at will, and came daily to the chief council chamber to meddle in government.

sentences.zh: 𣪝言：「黃門宦者之設，本以給事內庭，供掃除而已。

translations.literal: Jue said: "The establishment of eunuchs of the Yellow Gate was originally to serve the inner court and provide sweeping and cleaning alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue said, "Eunuchs of the Yellow Gate were originally created only to serve the inner palace and attend to menial tasks.

sentences.zh: 俾與政事，則貪暴無厭，待以兵權，則慘毒無已，皆前世已行之驗也。

translations.literal: If they are allowed to participate in government affairs, they become insatiably greedy and violent; if they are entrusted with military authority, their cruelty knows no end—all precedents from former ages have shown this.
translations.idiomatic: If they are allowed into government, they grow insatiably greedy and brutal; if they are given military command, their cruelty knows no bounds—history has proved this again and again.

sentences.zh: 故宦官用事於上，則生人受禍於下，匹夫力不能勝，則群起而攻之。

translations.literal: Therefore when eunuchs wield power above, the common people suffer calamity below; when a single man cannot overcome them by force, the masses rise up to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs hold power at court, the people below suffer; when ordinary men cannot defeat them alone, the masses rise up against them.

sentences.zh: 是以靖康之初，群起而攻之者庶民也；

translations.literal: Thus at the beginning of the Jingkang era those who rose up to attack them were commoners;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang reign it was commoners who rose against them;

sentences.zh: 睿聖皇帝南渡，駐蹕未安，群起而攻之者眾兵也。

translations.literal: when the Emperor Emeritus crossed south and the imperial residence was not yet secure, those who rose up to attack them were the mass of troops.
translations.idiomatic: when the retired emperor crossed south and the court had not yet settled, it was the soldiery who rose against them.

sentences.zh: 今當痛革前弊，並令選擇其人，曾經事任招權納寵者，屏之遠方，俾無浸淫以激眾怒，則賞罰之柄自朝廷出，國勢尊矣。

translations.literal: Now former abuses should be thoroughly reformed, and those selected should include only persons who have never held office by currying favor and seizing power; those who have should be banished to distant regions so that gradual encroachment may not provoke popular wrath—then the power of rewards and punishments will issue from the court and the state's dignity will be secured.
translations.idiomatic: We must now root out these abuses completely. Choose men carefully; anyone who has previously held office by currying favor and seizing power should be sent far away, lest gradual encroachment provoke the people's wrath. Then rewards and punishments will issue from the court alone, and the state's authority will be restored.

sentences.zh: 仍諭軍法便宜，止行於所轄軍伍， 其餘當聞之朝廷，付之有司，明正典刑，所以昭尊君之禮而全臣子忠義之節也。」

translations.literal: It should also be made clear that discretionary military law applies only within the troops under one's command; all other cases should be reported to the court, entrusted to the proper offices, and punished according to statute—thereby displaying the ritual of honoring the sovereign and preserving the integrity of loyal ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Commanders should also be told that discretionary military justice applies only within their own units; all other cases must be reported to the court and handled by the proper offices under established law. This will uphold the ritual of honoring the sovereign and preserve the integrity of loyal service."

sentences.zh: 疏留中不出。

translations.literal: The memorial was kept within and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was held back and not promulgated.

sentences.zh: 𣪝對，請付外行之。

translations.literal: Jue responded in audience and requested that it be sent out for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue responded in audience and asked that it be issued for implementation.

sentences.zh: 又論：「黃潛善、汪伯彥均於誤國，而潛善之罪居多，今同以散官竄謫湖南；

translations.literal: He also argued: "Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan both harmed the state, yet Qianshan's offenses were greater; now both are banished to Hunan with the same demoted rank;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan both harmed the state, yet Qianshan's guilt was the greater; now both are exiled to Hunan with the same reduced rank;

sentences.zh: 錢伯言與黃願皆棄城，呂源與梁揚祖皆擁兵而逃，今願罷官，揚祖落職，而源、伯言未正典刑，非所以勸懲。」

translations.literal: Qian Boyan and Huang Yuan both abandoned their cities; Lü Yuan and Liang Yangzu both fled with troops in hand. Now Yuan has been dismissed and Yangzu stripped of office, yet Yuan and Boyan have not been punished according to law—this is no way to encourage good conduct and warn against wrongdoing."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Boyan and Huang Yuan both abandoned their cities; Lü Yuan and Liang Yangzu both fled with their troops. Yuan has been dismissed and Yangzu stripped of office, yet Yuan and Boyan have not been punished under the law—this is no way to encourage loyalty or deter cowardice."

sentences.zh: 詔竄削有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered banishment and demotion in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered varying degrees of exile and demotion.

sentences.zh: 傅、正彥日至都堂議事，𣪝奏：「將帥之臣不可預政。」

translations.literal: Fu and Zhengyan came daily to the chief council chamber to discuss affairs; Jue memorialized: "Commanders must not participate in civil government."
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Zhengyan came daily to the chief council chamber to deliberate; Zheng Jue memorialized, "Military commanders must not take part in civil government."

sentences.zh: 及聞以簽書樞密院召呂頤浩，以禮部尚書召張浚，分張俊兵以五百人歸陝西，而浚不受尚書之命，俊不肯分所部兵，遂謫浚居郴州，擢俊以節度知鳳翔。

translations.literal: When it was heard that Lü Yihao was summoned as Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhang Jun as Minister of Rites, and five hundred of Zhang Jun's troops were to be sent back to Shaanxi, but Zhang Jun refused the ministerial appointment and Zhang Jun would not divide his forces, Zhang Jun was banished to Chenzhou and Zhang Jun was promoted to military commissioner governing Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Lü Yihao had been summoned as deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Zhang Jun as minister of rites, and that five hundred of Zhang Jun's troops were to be sent back to Shaanxi—but Zhang Jun refused the ministerial appointment and Zhang Jun would not divide his forces—Zhang Jun was exiled to Chenzhou while Zhang Jun was promoted to military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 𣪝知出二凶姦謀，具章乞留頤浩知金陵，浚不當貶，不報。

translations.literal: Jue knew this issued from the two villains' treacherous plot and submitted a full memorial requesting that Yihao be kept to govern Jinling and that Jun should not be demoted; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue saw that this came from the rebels' scheming and submitted a detailed memorial asking that Yihao be kept at Jinling and that Jun not be demoted; the court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 𣪝遂遣所親謝嚮變姓名，微服為賈人，徒步如平江見浚等，具言城中事，以為嚴設兵備，大張聲勢，持重緩進，使賊自遁，無驚動三宮，此上策也。

translations.literal: Jue then sent his close associate Xie Xiang, who changed his name, dressed as a common merchant, and went on foot to Pingjiang to see Jun and the others, reporting fully on affairs in the capital and advising that troops be arrayed in strict readiness, their strength displayed broadly, advance made deliberately and slowly so that the rebels would flee of themselves without disturbing the three palaces—this was the best strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue then sent his confidant Xie Xiang, who assumed another name, dressed as a merchant, and walked to Pingjiang to see Zhang Jun and the others. He reported fully on conditions in the capital and urged them to array their forces carefully, display great strength, and advance deliberately so that the rebels would withdraw on their own without alarming the imperial family—the best course, he said.

sentences.zh: 浚等聞之，皆感激奮厲為赴難計。

translations.literal: When Jun and the others heard this, all were moved and stirred to plans for rushing to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun and the others heard this, they were deeply moved and resolved to march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 俄詔睿聖皇帝為皇太弟、天下兵馬大元帥，幼主為皇太侄，即與大臣進議，以為：「在庭公卿、百司、群吏皆昔之臣屬也，今則與之比肩事主矣。

translations.literal: Soon an edict named the Emperor Emeritus Grand Imperial Younger Brother and Grand Marshal of All Armies, and the young sovereign Imperial Nephew; Jue immediately advanced discussion with the chief ministers, saying: "The dukes, ministers, and officials of every bureau in court were once their subjects; now they stand shoulder to shoulder serving the same lord.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict named the retired emperor grand imperial younger brother and commander of all armies, and the young emperor imperial nephew. Zheng Jue at once discussed the matter with the chief ministers, saying, "Every minister and official in court was once their subject; now they stand shoulder to shoulder serving the same lord.

sentences.zh: 稽之於古，則無所法；

translations.literal: Examined against antiquity, there is no precedent to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Measured against antiquity, there is no precedent;

sentences.zh: 行之於今，則實逆天。

translations.literal: applied in the present, it truly defies Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: applied today, it truly defies Heaven's order.

sentences.zh: 或者謂大元帥可以任軍旅之大事，臣竊以為不然。

translations.literal: Some say the Grand Marshal may be entrusted with great military affairs; your servant respectfully believes this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that the grand marshal may be entrusted with major military affairs, but I respectfully disagree.

sentences.zh: 昔舜之禪禹也，猶命禹徂征有苗，則禹雖受禪，而征伐之事舜猶親之也。

translations.literal: When Shun abdicated to Yu, he still ordered Yu to campaign against the Miao; thus though Yu received the abdication, Shun still personally directed military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun abdicated to Yu, he still ordered Yu to campaign against the Miao; though Yu had received the throne, Shun himself still directed military affairs.

sentences.zh: 唐睿宗傳位皇太子，以聽小事，自尊為太上皇，以聽大事。

translations.literal: When Tang Ruizong transferred the throne to the Crown Prince, the latter heard minor affairs while Ruizong styled himself Retired Emperor to hear major affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Ruizong passed the throne to the crown prince, the prince handled minor affairs while Ruizong took the title of retired emperor to handle major affairs.

sentences.zh: 如是無不可者，則稽之於古為有法，行之於今為得宜。」

translations.literal: If there is nothing improper in this, then examined against antiquity there is precedent, and applied in the present it is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: If that is done, there will be precedent in antiquity and propriety in the present."

sentences.zh: 太后垂簾同聽政，以安人心。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager should hold the curtain and jointly hear government to settle people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager should rule from behind the curtain to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 退與御史王庭秀上疏力爭。

translations.literal: He withdrew and, together with Censor Wang Tingxiu, submitted a memorial arguing forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and, together with Censor Wang Tingxiu, submitted a forceful joint memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 太后召𣪝與宰執同對簾前，𣪝乞召庭秀，太后諭曰：「今欲令睿聖皇帝總領兵馬爾。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned Jue and the chief ministers to answer before the curtain; Jue requested that Tingxiu also be summoned. The Empress Dowager instructed: "We now wish the Emperor Emeritus to take overall command of the armies."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned Zheng Jue and the chief ministers to audience behind the curtain. Zheng asked that Wang Tingxiu be summoned as well. The empress dowager said, "We now intend the retired emperor to take overall command of the armies."

sentences.zh: 𣪝奏曰：「臣不知其他，但人君位號豈容降改，聞之天下，孰不懷疑。

translations.literal: Jue memorialized: "Your servant knows nothing of other matters, but how can a sovereign's title and rank be lowered and changed? When this is heard throughout the realm, who will not harbor doubts?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue replied, "I know nothing of other matters, but how can a sovereign's titles be lowered and changed? When the world hears of it, who will not be filled with doubt?

sentences.zh: 雖前世衰亂分裂之時，固未有旬日之間易兩君，一朝降兩朝位號者也。」

translations.literal: Even in former ages of decline, chaos, and division, never within ten days were two rulers changed and two dynastic titles lowered in a single morning."
translations.idiomatic: Even in ages of decline and division, never within ten days were two rulers changed and two imperial titles lowered in a single morning."

sentences.zh: 太后令𣪝至都堂，朱勝非出朱昞等所上書以示𣪝、庭秀，𣪝、庭秀力言昨日詔書不可宣布，必召變。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered Jue to the chief council chamber; Zhu Shengfei produced memorials submitted by Zhu Bing and others to show Jue and Tingxiu; Jue and Tingxiu argued forcefully that yesterday's edict must not be promulgated, lest disaster be provoked.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent Zheng Jue to the chief council chamber. Zhu Shengfei produced memorials from Zhu Bing and others for Zheng and Wang to see. They argued forcefully that yesterday's edict must not be issued, warning that it would surely provoke disaster.

sentences.zh: 勝非與執政顏歧、王孝迪、路允迪皆在坐，尚書左丞張澄獨曰：「事勢若此，豈爭此名位耶？」

translations.literal: Shengfei and the chief administrators Yan Qi, Wang Xiaodi, and Lu Yundi were all present; Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Zhang Cheng alone said: "When affairs stand thus, why contend over these titles?"
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei and the chief administrators Yan Qi, Wang Xiaodi, and Lu Yundi were all present. Left vice minister Zhang Cheng alone said, "When affairs stand thus, why quarrel over titles?"

sentences.zh: 澂欲出，𣪝等共止之。

translations.literal: Cheng wished to leave; Jue and the others together stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng tried to leave, but Zheng Jue and the others together restrained him.

sentences.zh: 𣪝與李邴並為端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Jue and Li Bing were both made Academicians of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and jointly Deputy Directors of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue and Li Bing were both appointed academicians of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and joint deputy directors of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高宗復位，進簽書，執政甫百日而卒。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was restored to the throne, Jue was advanced to Deputy Director; he had been in office only a hundred days when he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was restored to the throne, Zheng was promoted to deputy director; he had served in high office barely a hundred days when he died.

sentences.zh: 高宗甚悼之，謂大臣：「朕喪元子，猶能自排遣，於𣪝殆不能釋也。」

translations.literal: Gaozong grieved deeply and told the ministers: "When I lost my eldest son I could still console myself, but over Jue I can scarcely find relief."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong grieved deeply and told his ministers, "When I lost my eldest son I could still console myself, but over Zheng Jue I can scarcely find peace."

sentences.zh: 王庭秀

translations.literal: Wang Tingxiu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiu

translations.literal: 〈Appended biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 庭秀，字潁彥，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Tingxiu, courtesy name Yingyan, was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiu, whose courtesy name was Yingyan, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 與黃庭堅、楊時遊，其為學旁搜遠紹，不苟趣時好，造詣深遠，操植堅正，發為文辭，俊邁宏遠。

translations.literal: He associated with Huang Tingjian and Yang Shi; in learning he searched broadly and traced distant sources, did not readily follow current fashions, attained profound depth, maintained upright conduct, and when he composed literary works they were lofty, vigorous, and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: He associated with Huang Tingjian and Yang Shi. In scholarship he ranged widely and drew on distant sources, refusing to chase current fashions. His attainments were profound and his conduct upright; his writings were lofty, vigorous, and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 登政和二年上舍第，歷官州縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe he passed the upper dormitory examination and served in posts in prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In 1112 he passed the upper dormitory examination and served in various prefectural and county posts.

sentences.zh: 侍御史李光薦為御史臺檢法官。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Li Guang recommended him as Reviewing Law Officer of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Li Guang recommended him as reviewing law officer of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 宣和、靖康時，進言皆發於忠義。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe and Jingkang eras, his memorials all sprang from loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe and Jingkang reigns, his memorials were invariably driven by loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞言：「偽楚時庶官中如虞謨、王庭秀者，初非疾病，毅然致為臣而歸，願褒擢之。」

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief said: "Among lower officials during the false Chu regime, such as Yu Mo and Wang Tingxiu, though not ill they resolutely resigned their posts as subjects and returned; it is hoped they may be praised and promoted."
translations.idiomatic: The vice censor-in-chief said, "Among lower officials during the puppet Chu regime, men such as Yu Mo and Wang Tingxiu were not ill but resolutely resigned their posts and returned to the Song. I ask that they be rewarded and promoted."

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，奏乞威斷當出於人主，而所遣宣諭官，當令舉廉吏。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor and memorialized requesting that decisive authority should issue from the sovereign, and that imperial envoys sent to announce edicts should be required to recommend incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor and memorialized that decisive authority must rest with the sovereign, and that imperial envoys should be required to recommend upright officials.

sentences.zh: 又言：「刑名有疑慮者，令州郡法官申憲司閱實具奏，以取裁決。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Where criminal cases raise doubts, let judges in prefectures and districts report to the surveillance commission for verification and memorialization to obtain a ruling."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Where criminal cases raise doubts, prefectural judges should report to the surveillance commission for verification and memorialization so that the court may decide."

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史，論黃潛善賣官售寵，罷之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attending Censor and impeached Huang Qianshan for selling offices and currying favor, leading to Qianshan's dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attending censor, impeached Huang Qianshan for selling offices and currying favor, and brought about his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 既與鄭𣪝力爭降封高宗事，未幾出知瑞州，右正言呂祉奏：「朝廷今日緣論大臣移一言官，明日罷一言官，則後日大臣行事有失，誰敢言者。」

translations.literal: After he and Zheng Jue had forcefully opposed demoting and enfeoffing Gaozong, before long he was sent out to govern Ruizhou. Right Remonstrance Officer Lü Zhi memorialized: "If today the court transfers a remonstrance officer because of a dispute with a chief minister, and tomorrow dismisses a remonstrance officer, then when chief ministers err hereafter, who will dare speak?"
translations.idiomatic: After he and Zheng Jue had forcefully opposed demoting Gaozong's titles, he was soon sent out to govern Ruizhou. Right remonstrance officer Lü Zhi memorialized, "If the court today transfers a remonstrance officer for disputing a minister, and tomorrow dismisses one, then when ministers err in future, who will dare speak up?"

sentences.zh: 遂召為吏部郎，改左司，言：「朝廷比來深疾貪吏，然州縣之間豈無廉介自將、沈於下僚者？

translations.literal: He was then recalled as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, transferred to the Left Department, and said: "The court has lately deeply detested corrupt officials, yet among prefectures and counties are there not men of integrity who keep themselves pure yet remain sunk in lower posts?
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as a director in the Ministry of Personnel and transferred to the Left Department. He said, "The court has lately hated corrupt officials, yet are there not upright men in the prefectures and counties who remain stuck in low posts?

sentences.zh: 宜命五使，所至以廉潔清修、可以師表吏民者，以名來上，參之公議，不次升擢，以厲士風。」

translations.literal: The five commissioners should be ordered that wherever they go, those who are incorrupt, pure in conduct, and able to serve as models for officials and people should have their names reported upward; after public discussion they should be promoted out of turn to encourage scholarly morale."
translations.idiomatic: The five commissioners should be instructed to report the names of officials who are incorrupt and exemplary wherever they travel; after public review they should be promoted out of turn to encourage upright conduct among scholars."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷檢正中書門下省諸房公事，與宰相議多不合，不自安，引疾求去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reviewing Administrator of the Secretariat-Chancellery Affairs in All Sections, often disagreed with the chief councilor in discussion, felt ill at ease, and cited illness to request dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to reviewing administrator of Secretariat-Chancellery affairs, often clashed with the chief councilor, felt uneasy, and cited illness to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔直秘閣、主管崇道觀而歸。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Direct Attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion and Superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey, and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named him direct attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion and superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey, and he retired.

sentences.zh: 仇悆，字泰然，益都人。

translations.literal: Chou Yu, courtesy name Tairan, was a native of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Yu, whose courtesy name was Tairan, came from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年進士，授邠州司法，讞獄詳恕，多所全活。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Judicial Officer of Bin Prefecture; in judging cases he was thorough and lenient and many lives were spared.
translations.idiomatic: In 1109 he earned his jinshi degree and was appointed judicial officer of Bin Prefecture. He judged cases with care and mercy, sparing many lives.

sentences.zh: 為鄧城令，滿秩，耆幼遮泣不得去。

translations.literal: As Magistrate of Dengcheng, when his term ended the old and young blocked his path weeping and would not let him leave.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Dengcheng, when his term ended the old and young blocked his path weeping and would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 徙武陟令，屬朝廷方調兵數十萬於燕山，悆饋餉畢給。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Wuzhi; at that time the court was mobilizing hundreds of thousands of troops at Yanshan, and Yu supplied provisions in full.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Wuzhi. The court was then mobilizing hundreds of thousands of troops at Yanshan, and Yu supplied their provisions in full.

sentences.zh: 時主將縱士卒過市掠物，不予直，他邑官逃避，悆先期趣備，申嚴約束，遂以不擾。

translations.literal: At that time the commanding general allowed soldiers to pass through the market plundering goods without paying fair price; officials of other counties fled, but Yu prepared in advance, enforced strict discipline, and thus the district was undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The commanding general then allowed his troops to plunder the markets without paying fair prices. Officials elsewhere fled, but Yu prepared in advance, enforced strict discipline, and kept his district undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 已而悆送運餉於涿，值大軍潰於盧溝河，囊橐往往委以資敵，悆間關營護，無一豪棄失。

translations.literal: Later Yu escorted transport provisions to Zhuo; the great army was routed at the Lugou River and baggage was often abandoned to supply the enemy, but Yu made his way through hardship to guard the convoy and not a single item was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later he escorted supply convoys to Zhuo. When the main army was routed at the Lugou River and baggage was abandoned everywhere to the enemy, Yu made his way through hardship guarding the convoy without losing a single item.

sentences.zh: 調高密丞，俗尚嚚訟，悆攝縣事，剖決如流，事無淹夕，民至懷餅餌以俟決遣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Gaomi; the custom favored vexatious litigation; Yu took charge of county affairs, decided cases like flowing water, and nothing remained overnight—people even brought cakes and pastries to await judgment and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Gaomi, where vexatious litigation was common. Acting magistrate, he decided cases with ease and cleared the docket each day; people brought cakes and pastries to await his judgments.

sentences.zh: 猾吏楊蓋每陰疏令過，脅持為姦，悆暴其罪黥之，無不悅服。

translations.literal: The crafty clerk Yang Gai often secretly reported the magistrate's faults and used them to extort and commit wrongdoing; Yu exposed his crimes and tattooed him as punishment, and none failed to rejoice and submit.
translations.idiomatic: The crafty clerk Yang Gai often secretly reported the magistrate's faults to extort and commit crimes. Yu exposed his crimes and had him tattooed as punishment, and everyone approved.

sentences.zh: 州闕司錄，命悆攝事，既行，邑氓萬餘邀留，至擁歸縣廨，時天寒，皆然火警守，布滿後先，悆由它道得出，或追拜馬首曰：「公舍我去，我必使公復來。」

translations.literal: The prefecture lacked a Registrar and Yu was ordered to act in that capacity; when he set out, more than ten thousand townspeople blocked his departure, even carrying him back to the county yamen; the weather was cold and all lit fires to keep watch, filling the roads before and behind; Yu escaped by another route, and some pursued to bow at his horse's head saying: "If you leave us, sir, we shall surely bring you back."
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture lacked a registrar, Yu was ordered to act in that post. As he set out, more than ten thousand townspeople blocked his way and even carried him back to the county yamen. In the cold weather they lit fires along the road to keep watch. Yu escaped by another route; some pursued him and bowed at his horse's head, saying, "If you leave us, sir, we shall surely bring you back."

sentences.zh: 它日，悆方白事郡牙，忽數千人徑奪以歸，守將弗能遏。

translations.literal: Another day, as Yu was reporting affairs at the prefectural gate, suddenly several thousand men seized him straight back; the defending commander could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Another day, as Yu was reporting to the prefectural office, several thousand men suddenly seized him and carried him back; the defending commander could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 劇寇起萊、密間，素聞悆名，戒其黨毋犯高密境，民賴以安。

translations.literal: Fierce bandits rose between Lai and Mi; having long heard Yu's name, they warned their followers not to violate Gaomi territory, and the people relied on this for security.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce bandits rose between Lai and Mi. Having long heard of Chou Yu's reputation, they warned their followers not to enter Gaomi, and the people were kept safe.

sentences.zh: 密卒閉關叛掠，害官吏幾盡，獨呼曰：「無驚仇公。」

translations.literal: Mi troops closed the passes in rebellion and plundered, killing officials almost to the last; they alone cried: "Do not alarm Master Chou."
translations.idiomatic: Mi troops closed the passes in rebellion, plundering and killing officials almost to the last man; they alone cried, "Do not harm Master Chou."

sentences.zh: 南遷，丁母憂。

translations.literal: When the court moved south, he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved south, he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，知建昌軍，入為考功員外。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he governed Jianchang Army and entered the capital as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Merit Section.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he governed Jianchang Army, then entered the capital as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel's merit section.

sentences.zh: 時仕者宛轉兵間，亡失告牒十常七八，而銓部無案籍，訴丐者甚多，真偽錯亂。

translations.literal: At that time officials wandered amid warfare; seven or eight in ten lost their appointment documents, yet the selection ministry had no records, and petitioners were many with truth and falsehood confused.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then wandered amid warfare; seven or eight in ten had lost their appointment documents, yet the selection ministry had no records. Petitioners were many and truth and falsehood were hopelessly confused.

sentences.zh: 悆親為考覈，其可據者悉責保識，因上聞行之。

translations.literal: Yu personally examined and verified them; those that could be substantiated were all required to provide guarantors, and this was reported upward and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Yu personally examined each case; those that could be verified were required to provide guarantors, and the system was reported to the throne and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 遷右司及中書門下檢正諸房公事，俄為沿海制置使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Right Department and Reviewing Administrator of Secretariat-Chancellery Affairs in All Sections, and soon became Coastal Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Right Department and reviewing administrator of Secretariat-Chancellery affairs, and soon became coastal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明守與宰相厚善，紿言士卒將為變，致遣精兵密捕。

translations.literal: The prefect of Ming was on close terms with the chief councilor and deceived him by saying the troops were about to mutiny, causing elite soldiers to be secretly sent to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Ming was close to the chief councilor and deceived him by claiming the troops were about to mutiny, causing elite soldiers to be sent in secret to arrest them.

sentences.zh: 統制官徐文覺之，初謀縱軍剽略，頃之泛海去，呼曰：「我以仇公故，不殺人，不焚屋廬。」

translations.literal: The controller Xu Wen perceived this; he had at first planned to let the army plunder, but soon sailed away across the sea, crying: "For Master Chou's sake I do not kill people or burn houses."
translations.idiomatic: The controller Xu Wen learned of this. He had at first planned to let his troops plunder, but soon sailed away across the sea, crying, "For Master Chou's sake I will not kill or burn houses."

sentences.zh: 一城晏然。

translations.literal: The whole city remained tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The whole city remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 猶坐削兩官，主管太平觀。

translations.literal: Yu was still punished by reduction of two ranks and appointment as Superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was still demoted two ranks and appointed superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 以淮西宣撫知廬州。

translations.literal: As Huaixi Pacification Commissioner he governed Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Huaixi pacification commissioner he governed Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉豫子麟合金兵大入，民情洶懼。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's son Lin joined Jin forces in a major invasion and popular sentiment was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's son Lin joined the Jin armies in a major invasion, and the people were greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 宣撫司統制張琦者，冀乘危為亂，驅居民越江南走。

translations.literal: The pacification commission's controller Zhang Qi hoped to take advantage of the crisis to create disorder and drove the residents to flee south across the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commission's controller Zhang Qi hoped to exploit the crisis to stir rebellion and drove the residents to flee south across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 欲先脅悆出，擁甲士數千突入，露刃登樓，揚白麾，左右驚潰，迫悆上馬。

translations.literal: He wished first to coerce Yu to flee, led several thousand armored soldiers in a sudden entry, bared blades and ascended the tower, waved a white banner, attendants fled in alarm, and Yu was forced onto a horse.
translations.idiomatic: He meant first to force Chou Yu to flee, led several thousand armored men in a sudden assault, bared their blades and climbed the tower, waved a white banner, and as attendants fled in panic forced Yu onto a horse.

sentences.zh: 悆徐謂曰：「若輩無守土責，吾當以死徇國，寇未至而逃，人何賴焉。」

translations.literal: Yu said calmly: "You have no responsibility to guard the territory; I shall die for the state. If we flee before the enemy arrives, whom can the people rely on?"
translations.idiomatic: Chou Yu said calmly, "You bear no duty to guard this territory. I shall die for the state. If we flee before the enemy even arrives, whom can the people rely on?"

sentences.zh: 堅不為動，神色無少異。

translations.literal: He firmly would not move, his expression showing not the slightest change.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to budge, his expression unchanged.

sentences.zh: 琦等錯愕，遽散其徒，人心遂定。

translations.literal: Qi and the others were startled and abashed and hastily dispersed their followers; popular sentiment was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi and his men were abashed and hastily dispersed their followers, and popular sentiment settled.

sentences.zh: 時金人出入近境，悆求援於宣撫司，不報。

translations.literal: At that time Jin troops moved in and out of the nearby borderlands; Yu requested aid from the pacification commission but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops were then moving in and out of the nearby borderlands. Chou Yu requested aid from the pacification commission but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 又遣其子自間道赴朝廷告急，雖旌其子以官，而援卒不至。

translations.literal: He also sent his son by a secret route to the court to report the emergency; though the son was rewarded with an office, relief troops never arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his son by a secret route to report the emergency to the court. Though his son was rewarded with an office, relief troops never came.

sentences.zh: 帝方下詔親征，而詔亦不至淮甸，喧言將棄兩淮為保江計。

translations.literal: The Emperor had just issued an edict for a personal campaign, yet the edict also did not reach the Huai region, and rumor spread that the two Huai districts would be abandoned to secure the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just issued an edict for a personal campaign, yet the edict never reached the Huai region, and rumor spread that the two Huai districts would be abandoned to secure the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 悆錄詔語揭之郡縣，讀者至流涕，咸思自奮。

translations.literal: Yu copied the edict's words and posted them in prefectures and counties; readers wept, and all wished to rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Yu copied the edict and posted it in the prefectures and counties. Readers wept, and all resolved to fight.

sentences.zh: 監押閻僅死於賊，餘眾來歸，州帑匱竭，無以為賞，悆悉引班坐，犒以酒食，慰勞之，眾皆感勵。

translations.literal: Supervisor Yan Jin died at the hands of bandits; the remaining troops came to submit. The prefectural treasury was exhausted and there was nothing for rewards; Yu had them all sit in ranks, entertained them with food and drink, and comforted them—and all were moved and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Yan Jin had died fighting bandits, and the survivors came in. The prefectural treasury was empty and there was nothing for rewards. Chou Yu had them all sit in ranks, feasted them with food and drink, and comforted them—and all were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 募廬、壽兵得數百，益鄉兵二千，出奇直抵壽春城下，敵三戰皆北，卻走度淮。

translations.literal: He recruited several hundred troops from Lu and Shou, added two thousand local militia, made a surprise attack straight to the walls of Shouchun, the enemy was defeated in three battles and retreated across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited several hundred troops from Lu and Shou, added two thousand local militia, and launched a surprise attack straight to Shouchun. The enemy was defeated in three battles and retreated across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 其後麟復增兵來寇，悆復壽春，俘馘甚眾，獲旗械數千，焚糧船百餘艘，降渤海首領二人。

translations.literal: Later Lin again increased troops to invade; Yu recovered Shouchun, took many captives and heads, seized thousands of banners and weapons, burned more than a hundred grain boats, and received the surrender of two Bohai chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lin again reinforced his army to invade. Chou Yu recovered Shouchun, took many prisoners and heads, seized thousands of banners and weapons, burned more than a hundred grain boats, and received the surrender of two Bohai chieftains.

sentences.zh: 初，金人圍濠州，旬日未下，屬天寒，馬多僵死，乃悉眾向淮東。

translations.literal: At first the Jin besieged Haozhou for ten days without taking it; as the weather turned cold many horses froze to death, and they then led all their forces toward Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Jin besieged Haozhou for ten days without success. The cold killed many of their horses, and they then marched their entire force toward Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 樞密使張浚方視師金陵，悆以策說之曰：「金重兵在淮東，師老食匱，若以精兵二萬一自壽陽，一自漢上，徑趨舊京，當不戰而退，繼以大軍尾擊，蔑有不濟者。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Zhang Jun was then inspecting troops at Jinling; Yu urged him with a plan: "The Jin have heavy forces in Huaidong; their army is weary and provisions exhausted. If twenty thousand elite troops—one column from Shouyang, one from the Han River—strike straight for the old capital, the enemy should withdraw without battle; then a great army can follow in pursuit, and nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau director Zhang Jun was then inspecting troops at Jinling. Chou Yu urged a plan on him: "The Jin have massed their army in Huaidong; their troops are weary and their supplies exhausted. Send twenty thousand elite troops—one column from Shouyang, one from the Han River—straight for the old capital, and the enemy should withdraw without a fight. Then follow with a larger army, and success is certain.

sentences.zh: 昔人謂『一日縱敵，數世之患』，願無失時之悔。」

translations.literal: The ancients said, 'Let the enemy go for a day and you suffer for generations'—may you not regret missing the moment."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that to let the enemy go for a day brings trouble for generations. Do not miss this moment and regret it later."

sentences.zh: 浚不能用。

translations.literal: Jun could not adopt the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun would not adopt the plan.

sentences.zh: 麟復以步騎數千至合肥，諜言兀朮為之殿，人心怖駭，不知所為。

translations.literal: Lin again came to Hefei with several thousand infantry and cavalry; spies reported that Wuzhu was covering the rear, and people's hearts were terrified, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Lin again advanced on Hefei with several thousand foot and horse. Spies reported that Wuzhu was covering the rear, and the people were terrified, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 會京西制置使遣牛皋統兵適至，悆顧左右曰：「召牛觀察來擊賊。」

translations.literal: It happened that the Jingxi Commissioner had sent Niu Gao leading troops just arriving; Yu turned to his attendants and said: "Summon Investigating Commissioner Niu to attack the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Jingxi commissioner sent Niu Gao with troops, who arrived in time. Chou Yu turned to his attendants and said, "Summon Commissioner Niu to attack the enemy."

sentences.zh: 皋既至，以忠義撼之，皋素勇甚，以二千餘騎馳出，短兵相接，所向披靡，敵稍懾，散而復集者三。

translations.literal: When Gao arrived, Yu stirred him with talk of loyalty and righteousness; Gao was always very brave and charged out with more than two thousand cavalry, closed in hand-to-hand, swept all before him, the enemy was somewhat cowed, and scattered and regathered three times.
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Gao arrived, Yu stirred him with talk of loyalty and righteousness. Niu Gao was famously brave and charged out with more than two thousand cavalry in close combat, sweeping all before him. The enemy wavered and scattered and regathered three times.

sentences.zh: 其副徐慶忽墜馬，敵競赴之，皋掖以上，手刜數人，因免胄大呼曰：「我牛皋也，嘗四敗兀朮，可來決死。」

translations.literal: His lieutenant Xu Qing suddenly fell from his horse and the enemy rushed upon him; Gao hauled him up, with his own hand cut down several men, then removed his helmet and cried loudly: "I am Niu Gao—I have four times defeated Wuzhu; come and fight to the death."
translations.idiomatic: His lieutenant Xu Qing suddenly fell from his horse and the enemy rushed at him. Gao pulled him up, cut down several men with his own hand, then removed his helmet and shouted, "I am Niu Gao! I have defeated Wuzhu four times—come and fight to the death!"

sentences.zh: 寇畏其名，遂自潰。

translations.literal: The bandits feared his name and thereupon broke and fled of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy feared his name and broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 以悆克復守禦功，加徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: For Yu's merit in recovering and defending the territory, he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Imperial Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in recovering and defending the territory, Chou Yu was promoted to attendant gentleman of the Hall of Imperial Proclamations.

sentences.zh: 明年，宣撫司始遣大將王德來，時寇已去，德謂其伍曰：「當事急時，吾屬無一人渡江擊賊，今事平方至，何面目見仇公耶？」

translations.literal: The next year the pacification commission at last sent the great general Wang De; the bandits had already gone. De said to his men: "When affairs were urgent not one of us crossed the river to strike the enemy; now that things are settled we arrive—what face have we to see Master Chou?"
translations.idiomatic: The next year the pacification commission at last sent the great general Wang De, but the enemy had already gone. Wang De said to his men, "When the crisis came, not one of us crossed the river to fight. Now that it is over we arrive—what face have we to show Master Chou?"

sentences.zh: 德麾下多女真、渤海歸附者，見悆像，不覺以手加額。

translations.literal: Many Jurchen and Bohai who had submitted were under De's command; seeing Yu's portrait, they unconsciously placed their hands on their foreheads.
translations.idiomatic: Many Jurchen and Bohai who had submitted served under Wang De. When they saw Chou Yu's portrait, they instinctively placed their hands on their foreheads in respect.

sentences.zh: 初，宣撫司既不以一卒援諸郡，但令焚積聚，棄城退保，文移不絕於道，又請浚督行之。

translations.literal: At first the pacification commission would not send a single soldier to aid the prefectures but only ordered stored goods burned and cities abandoned for defensive withdrawal; documents flowed unceasingly on the roads, and they also asked Jun to supervise enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: At first the pacification commission sent not a single soldier to aid the prefectures but only ordered supplies burned and cities abandoned. Documents flowed endlessly along the roads, and they also asked Zhang Jun to supervise enforcement.

sentences.zh: 浚檄悆度其宜處之，悆謂：「殘破之餘，兵食不給，誠不能支敵。

translations.literal: Jun sent a dispatch ordering Yu to judge what was appropriate; Yu said: "After devastation, troops and provisions are insufficient—we truly cannot withstand the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun ordered Chou Yu to judge what was appropriate. Yu replied, "After devastation we lack troops and provisions—we truly cannot withstand the enemy.

sentences.zh: 然帥臣任一路之責，誓當死守。

translations.literal: Yet a commander bears responsibility for a whole circuit and has sworn to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a commander bears responsibility for an entire circuit and has sworn to defend it to the death.

sentences.zh: 今若委城，使金人有淮西，治兵艦於巢湖，必貽朝廷憂。」

translations.literal: If we now abandon the city and let the Jin hold Huai west, building warships on Chaohu Lake, we will surely bring worry upon the court."
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon the city now and let the Jin hold western Huai and build warships on Chaohu Lake, we will surely bring grave worry upon the court."

sentences.zh: 力陳不可，浚韙其言，而卒全活數州之眾。

translations.literal: He argued forcefully that this could not be done; Jun approved his words, and in the end the populations of several prefectures were all preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: He argued forcefully against it. Zhang Jun approved his view, and in the end the populations of several prefectures were saved.

sentences.zh: 尋詔詣闕，軍民號送之。

translations.literal: Soon an edict summoned him to court; soldiers and civilians wept and escorted him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict summoned him to court, and soldiers and civilians wept as they escorted him on his way.

sentences.zh: 改浙東宣撫使、知明州，以挫豪強、獎善良為理。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhedong Pacification Commissioner and Governor of Ming Prefecture, governing by curbing the powerful and rewarding the good.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Zhedong pacification commissioner and governor of Ming Prefecture, governing by curbing the powerful and rewarding the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 吏受賕，雖一錢不貸，姦猾斂跡。

translations.literal: Officials who took bribes were not spared even for a single cash; the crafty and deceitful restrained their steps.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who took bribes were not spared even for a single coin, and the crafty and corrupt fell silent.

sentences.zh: 州罹兵火既燬，悆斥廚錢助其費，買田行鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: The prefecture had suffered war and fire and was already ruined; Yu spent kitchen funds to help cover expenses and bought land to conduct the village drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had been ravaged by war and fire. Yu spent his kitchen funds to help with expenses and bought land to conduct the village drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發官儲損其直，民無死徙。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he released government stores at reduced price, and the people had no deaths or migrations.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he released government grain at reduced prices, and the people suffered no deaths or migrations.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，進秩一等。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this, his rank was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of this, his rank was raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 再召，進對，帝親加褒諭，欲留置近密。

translations.literal: He was summoned again, advanced to audience, and the Emperor personally praised and instructed him, wishing to keep him close in confidential service.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again and advanced to audience. The emperor personally praised him and wished to keep him close at court.

sentences.zh: 言者以悆在郡多黥胥吏為慘酷，請授外藩。

translations.literal: Critics said Yu in the prefecture often tattooed clerks and was cruel, and requested that he be sent to an outer province.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said that in the prefecture Yu often tattooed clerks and was cruel, and asked that he be sent to an outer province.

sentences.zh: 時峒獠未息，乃進直學士，為湖南安撫使，禁盜鑄錢者，趣使為農，物價既平，商賈遂通。

translations.literal: At that time the cave tribes and Liao were not yet pacified; he was advanced to Direct Academician and made Hunan Pacification Commissioner, forbade illicit coiners, urged people to farm, prices were stabilized, and merchants then traveled freely.
translations.idiomatic: The cave tribes were not yet pacified. He was advanced to direct academician and made Hunan pacification commissioner, banned illicit coining, urged people to farm, stabilized prices, and commerce flourished.

sentences.zh: 數月，召還，加寶文閣學士、陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: After several months he was recalled, promoted to Academician of the Hall of Treasured Literature and Shaanxi Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was recalled and promoted to academician of the Hall of Treasured Literature and Shaanxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時金人無故歸侵疆，詭計叵測，悆力陳非策，固辭不行。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin without cause returned invaded territory; their schemes were unfathomable; Yu argued forcefully that this was no policy and firmly declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had without cause returned invaded territory, and their schemes were unfathomable. Yu argued forcefully that this was a bad policy and firmly refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 秦檜方主和議，以為異己，落職，以左朝奉郎、少府少監分司西京，全州居住。

translations.literal: Qin Hui was then directing the peace talks and regarded him as an opponent; Yu was demoted to Left Court Gentleman for Attendance, Vice Director of the Palace Workshops with nominal service at the Western Capital, and residence restricted to Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was directing the peace talks and regarded him as an opponent. Yu was demoted to left court gentleman for attendance and vice director of the Palace Workshops with nominal service at the Western Capital, and restricted to residence in Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 起知河南府，未行，金人果復陷所歸郡邑，如悆言。

translations.literal: He was raised to govern Henan Prefecture but had not yet departed when the Jin indeed again seized the returned prefectures and counties, just as Yu had said.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to govern Henan Prefecture but had not yet departed when the Jin indeed seized the returned prefectures and counties, just as Yu had predicted.

sentences.zh: 乃復待制，再知明州，改知平江府，陛辭，言：「我軍已習戰，非復前日，故劉錡能以少擊眾，敵大挫衄，若乘已振之勢，鼓行而前，中原可傳檄而定。」

translations.literal: He was then restored as Attendant Gentleman, again governed Ming Prefecture, and was transferred to govern Pingjiang Prefecture. At farewell audience he said: "Our army has grown accustomed to battle and is not as before; therefore Liu Qi could defeat many with few and the enemy suffered great defeat. If we ride this renewed momentum and march forward with drums, the Central Plains can be settled by proclamation alone."
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as attendant gentleman, again governed Ming Prefecture, and was transferred to Pingjiang Prefecture. At his farewell audience he said, "Our army has learned to fight and is no longer what it was. Liu Qi defeated a larger force with fewer men and the enemy suffered a great defeat. If we seize this renewed momentum and march forward, the Central Plains can be recovered by proclamation alone."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words.

sentences.zh: 以言罷，提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: Because of his words he was dismissed and made Superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his words he was dismissed and made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 積官至左朝議大夫，爵益都縣伯。

translations.literal: He accumulated offices to Left Policy Grandee and was ennobled as Baron of Yidu County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to left policy grandee and was ennobled as baron of Yidu County.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左通議大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Left Master of Policy.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title of left master of policy.

sentences.zh: 悆性至孝，母沒時，方崎嶇轉徙，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: Yu was supremely filial by nature; when his mother died he was amid arduous wanderings, yet he observed mourning with full ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was supremely filial. When his mother died amid the hardships of flight south, he still observed mourning with full ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 沿海制置使陳彥文薦於朝，起復之，悆不就。

translations.literal: Coastal Commissioner Chen Yanwen recommended him to the court and he was recalled from mourning, but Yu would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal commissioner Chen Yanwen recommended him to the court for recall from mourning, but Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 悆端方挺特，自初官訖通顯，無所附麗。

translations.literal: Yu was upright and outstanding; from his first office to high prominence he attached himself to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was upright and independent; from his first office to high rank he never attached himself to any faction.

sentences.zh: 令鄧城時，丞相范宗尹方為邑子，以文謁悆。

translations.literal: When he was Magistrate of Dengcheng, Chief Councilor Fan Zongyin was then a local youth and presented literary works to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When he was magistrate of Dengcheng, the future chief councilor Fan Zongyin was then a local youth and presented his writings to Yu.

sentences.zh: 悆他日語其父：「是子公輔器也。」

translations.literal: Yu one day told his father: "This son is material for chief minister and councilor."
translations.idiomatic: Yu one day told his father, "This boy has the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 宗尹既當國，未嘗以私見。

translations.literal: After Zongyin came to power, Yu never visited him privately.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongyin came to power, Yu never visited him for private favor.

sentences.zh: 悆在明州，嘗欲薦一幕官，問曰：「君日費幾何？」

translations.literal: When Yu was in Ming Prefecture he once wished to recommend a staff officer and asked: "How much do you spend daily?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was in Ming Prefecture he once wished to recommend a staff officer and asked, "How much do you spend each day?"

sentences.zh: 對以「十口之家，日用二千」。

translations.literal: He answered: "For a household of ten mouths, two thousand cash daily."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "For a household of ten, two thousand cash a day."

sentences.zh: 悆驚曰：「吾為郡守費不及此，屬僚所費倍之，安得不貪。」

translations.literal: Yu was startled and said: "As prefect my expenses do not reach this; subordinate officers spend twice as much—how can they not be corrupt?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu was startled and said, "As prefect my expenses do not reach that; a subordinate spending twice as much—how can he not be corrupt?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 高登，字彥先，漳浦人。

translations.literal: Gao Deng, courtesy name Yanxian, was a native of Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Deng, whose courtesy name was Yanxian, came from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，力學，持身以法度。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied diligently and conducted himself by law and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he studied hard and conducted himself by strict moral standards.

sentences.zh: 宣和間，為太學生。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe era he was a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe reign he was a student at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 金人犯京師，登與陳東等上書乞斬六賊。

translations.literal: When the Jin attacked the capital, Deng with Chen Dong and others submitted a memorial requesting execution of the Six Traitors.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked the capital, Gao Deng joined Chen Dong and others in a memorial demanding the execution of the Six Traitors.

sentences.zh: 廷臣復建和議，奪种師道、李綱兵柄，登與東再抱書詣闕，軍民不期而會者數萬。

translations.literal: Court ministers again proposed peace talks and stripped Zhong Shidao and Li Gang of military authority; Deng and Dong again carried petitions to the palace gate, and soldiers and civilians who gathered without prior arrangement numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers again proposed peace and stripped Zhong Shidao and Li Gang of military command. Deng and Dong again carried petitions to the palace, and tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians gathered spontaneously.

sentences.zh: 王時雍縱兵欲盡殲之，登與十人屹立不動。

translations.literal: Wang Shiyong unleashed troops intending to annihilate them completely; Deng and ten others stood firm without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyong unleashed troops to annihilate them, but Deng and ten others stood firm without moving.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，擢吳敏、張邦昌為相，敏又雪前相李邦彥無辜，乞加恩禮起復之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, Wu Min and Zhang Bangchang were promoted as chief councilors; Min also cleared the former chief councilor Li Bangyan of wrongdoing and requested favor and ritual for recall from dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, Wu Min and Zhang Bangchang were made chief councilors. Min also cleared the former chief councilor Li Bangyan of wrongdoing and asked that he be recalled with honors.

sentences.zh: 登上書曰：

translations.literal: Deng submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gao Deng submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 再上書曰：「臣以布衣之微賤，臣言繫宗社之存亡，未可忽也。」

translations.literal: He submitted another memorial saying: "Your servant is but a humble commoner in slight station; your servant's words bear on the survival or destruction of the altars of state and must not be neglected."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "I am but a humble commoner, yet my words bear on the survival of the state and must not be ignored."

sentences.zh: 於是凡五上書，皆不報。

translations.literal: In all he submitted five memorials, and none received reply.
translations.idiomatic: In all he submitted five memorials, and none received a reply.

sentences.zh: 因謀南歸，忽聞邦昌各與遠郡，一時小人相繼罷斥，與所言偶合者十七八，登喜曰：「是可以盡言矣。」

translations.literal: He therefore planned to return south; suddenly he heard that Bangchang had each been given distant prefectures and that petty men of the moment were dismissed one after another—seventeen or eight out of ten matching what he had said—and Deng rejoiced: "Now one may speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: He planned to return south. Suddenly he heard that Bangchang had been sent to distant prefectures and that petty men were being dismissed one after another—seventeen or eighteen matching what he had urged—and Deng rejoiced, "Now I may speak fully."

sentences.zh: 復為書論敏未罷，不報。

translations.literal: He again wrote arguing that Min had not been dismissed; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again arguing that Wu Min had not been dismissed; again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 初，金人至，六館諸生將遁去，登曰：「君在可乎？」

translations.literal: At first when the Jin arrived, students of the Six Halls were about to flee; Deng said: "While the sovereign is present, can we leave?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first arrived, students of the Six Halls were about to flee. Deng said, "While the sovereign is still here, can we leave?"

sentences.zh: 與林邁等請隨駕，隸聶山帳中，而帝不果出。

translations.literal: With Lin Mai and others he requested to follow the imperial progress and was attached to Nie Shan's camp, but the Emperor did not in the end depart.
translations.idiomatic: With Lin Mai and others he asked to follow the imperial progress and was attached to Nie Shan's camp, but the emperor did not depart in the end.

sentences.zh: 金人退師，敏遂諷學官起羅織，屏斥還鄉。

translations.literal: When the Jin withdrew their army, Min then prompted the academy officers to fabricate charges and had Deng expelled back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin withdrew, Min prompted the academy officers to fabricate charges and had Deng expelled to his home.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，廷對，極意盡言，無所顧避，有司惡其直，授富川主簿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, at the palace examination audience, he spoke his mind fully without regard for avoidance; the authorities hated his bluntness and appointed him Recorder of Fuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1132, at the palace examination audience, he spoke his mind fully without holding back. The authorities hated his bluntness and appointed him recorder of Fuchuan.

sentences.zh: 憲董弅聞其名，檄讞六郡獄，復命兼賀州學事。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Dong Bi heard his name and dispatched him to judge cases in six prefectures' prisons, then ordered him also to oversee Hezhou school affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Dong Bi heard of him and dispatched him to judge cases in six prefectures' prisons, then also put him in charge of Hezhou school affairs.

sentences.zh: 學故有田舍，法罷歸買馬司，登請復其舊。

translations.literal: The school originally had field estates; by regulation these had been abolished and returned to the Horse Purchasing Directorate; Deng requested restoration of the former arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The school had once owned field estates, but by regulation they had been transferred to the Horse Purchasing Directorate. Deng asked that the old arrangement be restored.

sentences.zh: 守曰：「買馬、養士孰急？」

translations.literal: The prefect said: "Buying horses and nurturing scholars—which is more urgent?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect said, "Buying horses and nurturing scholars—which is more urgent?"

sentences.zh: 登曰：「買馬固急矣，然學校禮義由出，一日廢，衣冠之士與堂下卒何異？」

translations.literal: Deng said: "Buying horses is indeed urgent, yet ritual and righteousness issue from the schools; once abandoned for a day, how are cap-and-gown scholars different from hall attendants?"
translations.idiomatic: Deng said, "Buying horses is urgent, but ritual and righteousness come from the schools. Once abandoned, how are scholars in cap and gown different from hall attendants?"

sentences.zh: 守曰：「抗長吏耶！」

translations.literal: The prefect said: "You defy your superior officer!"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect said, "You defy your superior!"

sentences.zh: 曰：「天下所恃以治者，禮義與法度 爾，既兩棄之，尚何言！」

translations.literal: He said: "What the realm relies on for order is ritual, righteousness, and law alone; having abandoned both, what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The realm relies on ritual, righteousness, and law for order. Having abandoned both, what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 守不能奪，卒從之。

translations.literal: The prefect could not change his mind and in the end followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect could not prevail and in the end agreed.

sentences.zh: 攝獄事，有囚殺人，守欲奏裁曰：「陰德可為。」

translations.literal: While acting in prison affairs, a prisoner had committed murder; the prefect wished to memorialize for discretionary judgment, saying: "Hidden merit may be performed."
translations.idiomatic: While handling prison affairs, a prisoner had committed murder. The prefect wished to memorialize for discretionary leniency, saying, "One may perform hidden merit."

sentences.zh: 登曰：「陰德豈可有心為之，殺人者死，而可幸免，則被死之冤何時而銷？」

translations.literal: Deng said: "How can hidden merit be performed with deliberate intent? Those who kill shall die; if they may escape punishment, when will the wrong of those who were killed be redressed?"
translations.idiomatic: Deng said, "Hidden merit cannot be performed with deliberate intent. Murderers must die. If they escape punishment, when will the wrong done to the victims be redressed?"

sentences.zh: 滿秩，士民丐留不獲，相率饋金五十萬，不告姓名，白於守曰：「高君貧無以養，願太守勸其咸受。」

translations.literal: When his term ended, scholars and people begged to keep him but failed; they together presented five hundred thousand cash without giving their names and informed the prefect: "Master Gao is poor and cannot support himself; we ask the prefect to urge him to accept all."
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, scholars and commoners begged to keep him but failed. They together presented five hundred thousand cash without giving their names and told the prefect, "Master Gao is poor and cannot support himself. We ask the prefect to urge him to accept it all."

sentences.zh: 登辭之，不可，復無所歸，請置於學，買書以謝士民。

translations.literal: Deng declined but could not refuse; having nowhere else to put it, he asked that it be placed with the school and used to buy books to thank scholars and people.
translations.idiomatic: Deng declined but could not refuse. With nowhere else to put the money, he placed it with the school and bought books to thank the people.

sentences.zh: 歸至廣，會新興大饑，帥連南夫檄發廩振濟，復為糜於野以食之，願貸者聽，所全活萬計。

translations.literal: Returning to Guang, he encountered great famine in Xinxing; Commander Lian Nanfu dispatched orders to open granaries for relief; Deng also made gruel in the fields to feed people, allowed those who wished to borrow grain, and those preserved alive numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Guang, he encountered severe famine in Xinxing. Commander Lian Nanfu ordered granaries opened for relief. Deng also made gruel in the fields to feed people, allowed borrowing of grain, and saved tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 歲適大稔，而償亦及數。

translations.literal: That year happened to be a great harvest, and repayment also reached the expected amount.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a great harvest, and repayment also reached the expected amount.

sentences.zh: 民投牒願留者數百輩，因奏辟終其任。

translations.literal: Several hundred people submitted petitions wishing to keep him, and he was therefore memorialized for appointment to complete his term.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred people submitted petitions asking to keep him, and he was memorialized for appointment to complete his term.

sentences.zh: 召赴都堂審察，遂上疏萬言及《時議》六篇，帝覽而善之，下六議中書。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the chief council hall for examination, then submitted a ten-thousand-word memorial and six chapters of "Contemporary Discussions"; the Emperor read them and approved, and sent the six discussions to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the chief council hall for examination and submitted a ten-thousand-word memorial and six chapters of Contemporary Discussions. The emperor read them with approval and sent the six chapters to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秦檜惡其譏己，不復以聞。

translations.literal: Qin Hui hated that he had satirized him and no longer reported them upward.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui hated that Deng had criticized him and no longer reported the memorials to the throne.

sentences.zh: 授靜江府古縣令，道湖州，守汪藻館之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Guxian in Jingjiang Prefecture; passing through Huzhou, Prefect Wang Zao lodged him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Guxian in Jingjiang Prefecture. Passing through Huzhou, Prefect Wang Zao lodged him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 藻留與修《徽宗實錄》，固辭，或曰：「是可以階改秩。」

translations.literal: Zao kept him to help compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Huizong; he firmly declined. Someone said: "This could serve as a step to change rank."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao asked him to stay and help compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Huizong, but he firmly declined. Someone said, "That could advance your rank."

sentences.zh: 登曰：「但意未欲爾。」

translations.literal: Deng said: "It is only that my intent does not wish it."
translations.idiomatic: Deng said, "I simply do not wish to."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He then departed.

sentences.zh: 廣西帥沈晦問登何以治縣，登條十餘事告之。

translations.literal: Guangxi Commander Shen Hui asked Deng how to govern a county; Deng listed more than ten matters and told him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi commander Shen Hui asked Deng how to govern a county. Deng listed more than ten points.

sentences.zh: 晦曰：「此古人之政，今人詐，疑不可行。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "This is government of the ancients; people today are deceitful—I doubt it can be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hui said, "That is the government of the ancients. People today are deceitful—I doubt it can work."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「忠信可行蠻貊，謂不能行，誠不至爾。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Loyalty and faithfulness can be practiced even among barbarians of the south and north; to say it cannot be done means sincerity has not yet reached that point."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Loyalty and sincerity can prevail even among barbarians. To say it cannot work means one's sincerity has not yet been sufficient."

sentences.zh: 豪民秦琥武斷鄉曲，持吏短長，號「秦大蟲」，邑大夫以下為其所屈。

translations.literal: The powerful local Qin Hu tyrannized the countryside, held officials' faults over them, and was called "Great Worm Qin"; district grandees and below were bent by him.
translations.idiomatic: The local bully Qin Hu tyrannized the countryside, held officials' faults over them, and was called "Great Worm Qin." District officials below the magistrate all bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 登至，頗革，而登喜其遷善，補處學職。

translations.literal: When Deng arrived, Hu changed considerably; Deng was pleased at his turning toward goodness and appointed him to a school post.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng arrived, Qin Hu changed considerably. Deng was pleased at his turning toward goodness and gave him a school post.

sentences.zh: 它日，琥有請屬，登謝卻之，琥怒，謀中以危法。

translations.literal: Another day Hu made a request for favor; Deng politely refused; Hu grew angry and plotted to trap him with a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Qin Hu asked a favor. Deng politely refused. Qin Hu grew angry and plotted to trap him with a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 會有訴琥侵貸學錢者，登呼至，面數琥，聲氣俱厲，叱下，白郡及諸司置之法，忿而死，一郡快之。

translations.literal: It happened that someone sued Hu for embezzling school funds; Deng summoned him, rebuked Hu to his face with voice and manner both stern, shouted him down, reported to the prefecture and various offices to punish by law; Hu died of resentment and the whole prefecture rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then sued Qin Hu for embezzling school funds. Deng summoned him, rebuked him to his face in a thunderous voice, shouted him down, and reported to the prefecture and various offices to punish him by law. Qin Hu died of rage and the whole prefecture rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 帥胡舜陟謂登曰：「古縣，秦太師父舊治，實生太師於此，盍祠祀之？」

translations.literal: Commander Hu Shunzhi said to Deng: "Guxian was the old jurisdiction of Grand Preceptor Qin's father; the Grand Preceptor was in fact born here—why not establish a shrine to worship him?"
translations.idiomatic: Commander Hu Shunzhi said to Deng, "Guxian was where Grand Preceptor Qin's father once governed, and the grand preceptor was born here. Why not establish a shrine to worship him?"

sentences.zh: 登曰：「檜為相亡狀，祠不可立。」

translations.literal: Deng said: "When Hui was chief councilor his conduct was deplorable—a shrine must not be established."
translations.idiomatic: Deng said, "When Qin Hui was chief councilor his conduct was deplorable. A shrine must not be established."

sentences.zh: 舜陟大怒，摭秦琥事，移荔浦丞康寧以代登，登以母病去。

translations.literal: Shunzhi was greatly angered, seized on the Qin Hu affair, transferred Lipu Assistant Magistrate Kang Ning to replace Deng, and Deng left because of his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi was furious, seized on the Qin Hu affair, transferred Lipu assistant magistrate Kang Ning to replace Deng, and Deng left because of his mother's illness.

sentences.zh: 舜陟遂創檜祠而自為記，且誣以專殺之罪，詔送靜江府獄。

translations.literal: Shunzhi then founded a shrine to Hui and wrote the inscription himself, and also falsely charged Deng with unauthorized killing; an edict ordered him sent to Jingjiang Prefecture prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi then founded a shrine to Qin Hui and wrote the inscription himself, and also falsely charged Deng with unauthorized killing. An edict ordered him sent to Jingjiang prison.

sentences.zh: 舜陟遣健卒捕登，屬登母死舟中，藁葬水次，航海詣闕上書，求納官贖罪，帝閔之。

translations.literal: Shunzhi sent strong soldiers to arrest Deng; it happened that Deng's mother died on the boat; he buried her in straw rites at the water's edge, sailed by sea to the court to submit a memorial, and requested to surrender office to redeem guilt; the Emperor pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi sent strong soldiers to arrest Deng. Deng's mother died on the boat; he buried her in a simple rite at the water's edge, sailed to court to submit a memorial, and asked to surrender his office to redeem his guilt. The emperor pitied him.

sentences.zh: 故人有為右司者，謂曰：「丞相云嘗識君於太學，能一見，終身事且無憂，上書徒爾為也。」

translations.literal: An old acquaintance who served in the Right Department said to him: "The chief councilor says he once knew you at the Imperial Academy; if you can see him once, affairs for life will be without worry—submitting memorials is vain effort."
translations.idiomatic: An old friend in the Right Department said to him, "The chief councilor says he knew you at the Imperial Academy. If you see him once, you will have nothing to worry about for life. Memorials are useless."

sentences.zh: 登曰：「某知有君父，不知有權臣。」

translations.literal: Deng said: "I know there is a sovereign and father; I do not know there are powerful ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Deng said, "I know my sovereign and father; I do not know powerful ministers."

sentences.zh: 既而中書奏故事無納官贖罪，仍送靜江獄。

translations.literal: The Secretariat then memorialized that precedent had no surrender of office to redeem guilt, and he was still sent to Jingjiang prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then reported that precedent had no provision for surrendering office to redeem guilt, and he was still sent to Jingjiang prison.

sentences.zh: 登歸葬其母，訖事詣獄，而舜陟先以事下獄死矣，事卒昭白。

translations.literal: Deng returned to bury his mother; when the rites were finished he went to prison, but Shunzhi had already been imprisoned on other charges and died; the matter was finally cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Deng returned to bury his mother. When the rites were finished he went to prison, but Shunzhi had already been imprisoned on other charges and died. The matter was finally cleared.

sentences.zh: 廣漕鄭鬲、趙不棄辟攝歸善令，遂差考試，摘經史中要語命題，策閩、浙水災所致之由。

translations.literal: Guang Transport Commissioners Zheng Ge and Zhao Buqi appointed him acting Magistrate of Guishan; he was then assigned to conduct examinations, selecting key passages from the classics and histories for topics, and examined on the causes of flooding disasters in Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guang transport commissioners Zheng Ge and Zhao Buqi appointed him acting magistrate of Guishan. He was then assigned to conduct examinations, drawing topics from key passages in the classics and histories, and set a question on the causes of flooding in Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 郡守李仲文即馳以達檜，檜聞震怒，坐以前事，取旨編管容州。

translations.literal: Prefect Li Zhongwen immediately sent it by urgent dispatch to Hui; when Hui heard he was shaken with rage, and on the basis of former affairs obtained an edict to register and confine Deng in Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Zhongwen immediately sent it by urgent dispatch to Qin Hui. When Hui heard, he was furious and, on the basis of former affairs, obtained an edict to confine Deng in Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 漳州遣使臣謝大作持省符示登，登讀畢，即投大作上馬，大作曰：「少入告家人，無害也。」

translations.literal: Zhangzhou sent envoy Xie Dazuo bearing provincial documents to show Deng; when Deng had finished reading he immediately mounted Dazuo's horse; Dazuo said: "Go in briefly to tell your family—no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou sent envoy Xie Dazuo with provincial documents for Deng. When Deng finished reading, he immediately mounted Dazuo's horse. Dazuo said, "Go in briefly to tell your family—it will do no harm."

sentences.zh: 登曰：「君命不敢稽。」

translations.literal: Deng said: "I dare not delay the sovereign's command."
