translations.idiomatic: Deng said, "I dare not delay the sovereign's command."

sentences.zh: 大作愕然。

translations.literal: Dazuo was startled.
translations.idiomatic: Dazuo was startled.

sentences.zh: 比夜，巡檢領百卒復至，登曰：「若朝廷賜我死，亦當拜敕而後就法。」

translations.literal: By night the patrol officer led a hundred soldiers and came again; Deng said: "If the court grants me death, I should still receive the edict with obeisance before submitting to the law."
translations.idiomatic: By night the patrol officer returned with a hundred soldiers. Deng said, "If the court orders my death, I should still receive the edict with obeisance before submitting to the law."

sentences.zh: 大作感登忠義，為泣下，奮劍叱巡檢曰：「省符在我手中，無它語也。

translations.literal: Dazuo was moved by Deng's loyalty and righteousness, wept, brandished his sword and shouted at the patrol officer: "The provincial document is in my hands—there is nothing else to say.
translations.idiomatic: Dazuo was moved by Deng's loyalty, wept, brandished his sword, and shouted at the patrol officer, "The provincial document is in my hands—there is nothing else to say.

sentences.zh: 汝欲何為，吾當以死捍之。」

translations.literal: What do you intend? I shall defend him with my life."
translations.idiomatic: What do you intend? I shall defend him with my life."

sentences.zh: 鬲、不棄亦坐鐫一官。

translations.literal: Ge and Buqi were also punished by reduction of one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ge and Buqi were also demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 登謫居，授徒以給，家事一不介意，惟聞朝廷所行事小失，則顰蹙不樂，大失則慟哭隨之，臨卒，所言皆天下大計。

translations.literal: Deng lived in banishment, teaching pupils for support, heedless of household affairs; only when he heard the court commit small errors he frowned and was displeased, and when great errors occurred he followed with wailing grief; nearing death, his words were all great plans for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Deng lived in exile, teaching pupils for a living and caring nothing for household affairs. When he heard the court commit small errors he frowned with displeasure; when great errors occurred he wept. Near death, his words were all great plans for the realm.

sentences.zh: 後二十年，丞相梁克家疏其事以聞。

translations.literal: Twenty years later Chief Councilor Liang Kejia memorialized the matter to inform the court.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later Chief Councilor Liang Kejia memorialized the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 何萬守漳，言諸朝，追復迪功郎。

translations.literal: He Wan governed Zhangzhou, spoke of it at court, and Deng was posthumously restored as Diligent Merit Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He Wan, prefect of Zhangzhou, spoke of it at court, and Deng was posthumously restored as diligent merit gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後五十年，朱熹為守，奏乞褒錄，贈承務郎。

translations.literal: Fifty years later Zhu Xi was prefect and memorialized requesting praise and record; Deng was granted Attendant Gentleman for Affairs posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty years later Zhu Xi was prefect and memorialized requesting official recognition. Deng was posthumously granted attendant gentleman for affairs.

sentences.zh: 登事其母至孝，舟行至封、康間，阻風，方念無以奉晨膳，忽有白魚躍於前。

translations.literal: Deng served his mother with supreme filial piety; traveling by boat between Feng and Kang, blocked by wind, he was just thinking he had nothing for the morning meal when suddenly a white fish leaped before him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng served his mother with supreme filial piety. Traveling by boat between Feng and Kang, he was blocked by wind and worried he had nothing for her morning meal when a white fish suddenly leaped before him.

sentences.zh: 其學以慎獨為本，所著《家論》、《忠辨》等編，有《東溪集》行世。

translations.literal: His learning took cautious solitude as foundation; works he authored include "Household Discourses" and "Discrimination of Loyalty" and others; his "Collected Works of East Creek" circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His learning took cautious solitude as its foundation. He authored Household Discourses, Discrimination of Loyalty, and other works; his Collected Works of East Creek circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 婁寅亮

translations.literal: Lou Yinliang
translations.idiomatic: Lou Yinliang

sentences.zh: 婁寅亮，字陟明，永嘉人。

translations.literal: Lou Yinliang, courtesy name Zhiming, was a native of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Yinliang, whose courtesy name was Zhiming, came from Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 政和二年進士，為上虞丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe he passed the jinshi examination and served as Assistant Magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1112 he earned his jinshi degree and served as assistant magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，高宗至越，寅亮上疏云：

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan, when Gaozong reached Yue, Yinliang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In 1130, when Gaozong reached Yue, Yinliang submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「先正有言：『太祖舍其子而立弟，此天下之大公；

translations.literal: " A former worthy said: 'Taizu set aside his son and established his younger brother—this was the great public-mindedness of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: " A former worthy said, "Taizu set aside his son and established his younger brother—this was the great public-mindedness of the realm;

sentences.zh: 周王薨，章聖取宗室育之宮中，此天下之大慮也。』

translations.literal: when Prince Zhou died, Zhangsheng took a clansman and raised him in the palace—this was the great forethought of the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: when Prince Zhou died, Emperor Zhangsheng took a clansman and raised him in the palace—this was the great forethought of the realm."

sentences.zh: 仁宗感悟其說，詔英祖入繼大統。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was moved by this doctrine and ordered Emperor Yingzu to enter and succeed to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was moved by this doctrine and ordered Emperor Yingzu to succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 文子文孫，宜君宜王，遭罹變故，不斷如帶。

translations.literal: Cultured sons and cultured grandsons, fit to be rulers and kings, suffered calamities, cut off like a belt's end.
translations.idiomatic: His cultured sons and grandsons, fit to rule as kings, suffered calamity and were cut off like a severed belt.

sentences.zh: 今有天下者，獨陛下一人而已。

translations.literal: He who now possesses the realm is Your Majesty alone.
translations.idiomatic: He who now possesses the realm is Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 屬者椒寢未繁，前星不耀，孤立無助，有識寒心。

translations.literal: Lately the inner quarters have not flourished, the former star does not shine, you stand alone without aid, and the discerning are chilled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the inner quarters have not flourished, the heir apparent does not shine, you stand alone without aid, and the discerning are chilled at heart.

sentences.zh: 天其或者深戒陛下，追念祖宗公心長慮之所及乎？

translations.literal: Has Heaven perhaps deeply admonished Your Majesty to recall what the ancestors' public-mindedness and long forethought reached?
translations.idiomatic: Has Heaven perhaps deeply admonished Your Majesty to recall the public-mindedness and long forethought of your ancestors?

sentences.zh: 崇寧以來，諛臣進說，獨推濮王子孫以為近屬，餘皆謂之同姓，遂使昌陵之後，寂寥無聞，奔迸藍縷，僅同民庶。

translations.literal: Since Chongning, fawning ministers advanced doctrines, promoting only descendants of Prince Pu as close kin while all others were called same-surname clansmen; thus descendants of Changling were lonely and unheard of, fleeing in tattered dress scarcely different from common people.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Chongning era, fawning ministers have promoted only descendants of Prince Pu as close kin while calling all others mere same-surname clansmen. Thus Taizu's descendants have been forgotten, fleeing in rags scarcely different from commoners.

sentences.zh: 恐祀豐於昵，仰違天監，太祖在天莫肯顧歆，是以二聖未有回鑾之期，金人未有悔禍之意，中原未有息肩之日。

translations.literal: I fear sacrifices are abundant for the near at hand but violate Heaven's regard above; Taizu in Heaven will not deign to look down with favor—therefore the two sovereigns have no date for returning the imperial carriage, the Jin have no intent to repent their calamities, and the Central Plains have no day of resting their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: I fear sacrifices favor the near at hand but violate Heaven's regard, and Taizu in Heaven will not look down with favor. Therefore the two emperors have no date of return, the Jin show no intent to repent, and the Central Plains have no day of rest.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不識忌諱，欲乞陛下於子行中遴選太祖諸孫有賢德者，視秩親王，俾牧九州，以待皇嗣之生，退處藩服，並選宣祖、太宗之裔，材武可稱之人，升為南班，以備環衛。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant does not know taboo and wishes to beg Your Majesty to select among the sons' generation a worthy Taizu grandson of virtuous conduct, treat his rank as imperial prince, let him govern the nine provinces while awaiting the birth of the imperial heir, then retire to princely status; and also select descendants of Emperor Xuanzu and Emperor Taizong of martial talent fit for praise, promote them to the southern ranks, and prepare them for palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant does not know taboo and begs Your Majesty to select a worthy grandson of Taizu from among the princes, treat him as an imperial prince, and let him govern the realm while awaiting the birth of an heir, then retire to princely status. Also select descendants of Xuanzu and Taizong of proven martial talent for the southern ranks as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 庶幾上慰在天之靈，下係人心之望。」

translations.literal: Perhaps thereby comforting the spirits in Heaven above and binding the people's hopes below."
translations.idiomatic: Thus comforting the spirits in Heaven and binding the people's hopes."

sentences.zh: 帝讀之感悟，樞密富直柔薦之。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and was moved to understanding; Bureau Director Fu Zhirou recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and was deeply moved; bureau director Fu Zhirou recommended him.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，召赴行在，以其言宗社大計也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he was summoned to the mobile court because his words concerned the great plan of altars and state.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 he was summoned to the mobile court because his words concerned the survival of the state.

sentences.zh: 既入見，復上疏曰：

translations.literal: After entering audience he again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: After entering audience he again submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「陛下轍迹所環，六年於外，險阻艱難，備嘗之矣。

translations.literal: " Your Majesty's wheel tracks have ranged abroad six years; dangers, obstacles, and hardships—you have tasted them all.
translations.idiomatic: " Your Majesty has been abroad six years and has tasted every danger and hardship.

sentences.zh: 然而二聖未還，金人未滅，四方未靖者，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet the two sovereigns have not returned, the Jin have not been destroyed, and the four quarters are not pacified—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two emperors have not returned, the Jin are not destroyed, and the realm is not pacified—why?

sentences.zh: 天意若曰：天祚宋德，太祖不私其子而保之，不幸姦邪誤國而壞之，將使嗣聖念祖，思危而後獲之，乃所以申其永命也。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent seems to say: Heaven blesses Song virtue; Taizu did not favor his own son but preserved the realm; unhappily treacherous villains misled the state and ruined it; the succeeding sage will be made to remember the ancestors, think of peril and then attain restoration—this is how its everlasting mandate is extended.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent seems to be: Heaven blesses the Song; Taizu did not favor his own son but preserved the realm; treacherous villains misled the state and ruined it; the succeeding sage must remember the ancestors, heed peril, and then attain restoration—thus extending its everlasting mandate.

sentences.zh: 臣誠狂妄，去歲上章，請陛下取太祖諸孫之賢者，視秩親王，使牧九州，誤蒙采聽，赦而不誅。

translations.literal: Your servant is truly reckless; last year he submitted a memorial requesting Your Majesty to take a worthy Taizu grandson, treat his rank as imperial prince, and let him govern the nine provinces; he mistakenly received adoption and hearing and was pardoned rather than executed.
translations.idiomatic: I was truly reckless. Last year I requested that Your Majesty select a worthy grandson of Taizu, treat him as an imperial prince, and let him govern the realm. I was mistakenly heard and pardoned rather than executed.

sentences.zh: 茲蓋在天之靈發悟聖心，為社稷計，非愚臣之所及也。

translations.literal: This surely is the spirits in Heaven awakening the sage heart for the altars and state—not something your foolish servant could reach.
translations.idiomatic: This surely is the spirits in Heaven awakening Your Majesty's heart for the sake of the state—not something I could have achieved.

sentences.zh: 伏望宣告大臣行之，它日皇子之生，使之退處清暇，不過增一節度使爾。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will proclaim this for the chief ministers to carry out; when a prince is born hereafter, let him retire to leisurely seclusion—it would be no more than adding one military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will proclaim this for the chief ministers to carry out. When a prince is born hereafter, let him retire to leisure—it would mean no more than adding one military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陛下以太祖之心，行章聖之慮，自然孝弟感通，兩宮回蹕，澤流萬世。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty with Taizu's heart carries out Zhangsheng's forethought, filial piety and brotherly duty will naturally move Heaven and earth, the two palaces will return their imperial progress, and blessings will flow for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty with Taizu's heart carries out Zhangsheng's forethought, filial piety will naturally move Heaven, the two palaces will return, and blessings will flow for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 改令入官，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to enter official service by order and promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to enter official service and promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時相秦檜以其直柔所薦，惡之，諷言者論寅亮匿父喪不舉，下大理鞫問，無實，猶坐為族父冒占官戶罷職，送吏部，由是坐廢。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Qin Hui, whom Zhirou had recommended for his bluntness, hated him; he prompted critics to impeach Yinliang for concealing his father's death without reporting mourning; the case went to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation and was unfounded, yet he was still punished for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register, dismissed, and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilor Qin Hui, whom Fu Zhirou had recommended, hated him and prompted critics to charge Yinliang with concealing his father's death. The Court of Judicial Review found no truth in it, yet he was still dismissed for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.

sentences.zh: 宋汝為

translations.literal: Song Ruwei
translations.idiomatic: Song Ruwei

sentences.zh: 時劉豫節制東平，丞相呂頤浩因致書豫。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu controlled Dongping; Chief Councilor Lü Yihao therefore sent a letter to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yu controlled Dongping, and chief councilor Lü Yihao sent him a letter.

sentences.zh: 汝為行次壽春，遇完顏宗弼軍，不克與時亮會，獨馳入其壁，將上國書。

translations.literal: Ruwei traveled and stopped at Shouchun, encountered the army of Wanyan Zongbi, could not join Shi Liang, and alone galloped into their camp to present the state letter.
translations.idiomatic: Ruwei stopped at Shouchun, encountered Wanyan Zongbi's army, could not join Shi Liang, and alone galloped into the enemy camp to present the state letter.

sentences.zh: 宗弼盛怒，劫而縛之，欲加僇辱。

translations.literal: Zongbi was greatly enraged, seized and bound him, and wished to add insult and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi was furious, seized and bound him, and meant to humiliate him.

sentences.zh: 汝為一無懼色，曰：「死固不辭，然銜命出疆，願達書吐一辭，死未晚。」

translations.literal: Ruwei showed not a trace of fear and said: "Death I do not refuse, yet bearing command beyond the border, I wish to deliver the letter and speak one word—death would not be too soon."
translations.idiomatic: Ruwei showed no fear and said, "I do not refuse death, but bearing command beyond the border I wish to deliver the letter and speak one word—then death would not be too soon."

sentences.zh: 宗弼顧汝為不屈，遂解縛延之曰：「此山東忠義之士也。」

translations.literal: Zongbi saw that Ruwei would not yield, then untied his bonds and received him, saying: "This is a loyal and righteous man of Shandong."
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi saw that Ruwei would not yield, untied his bonds, and received him, saying, "This is a loyal and righteous man of Shandong."

sentences.zh: 命往見豫，汝為曰：「願伏劍為南朝鬼，豈忍背主不忠於所事。」

translations.literal: He ordered him to go see Yu; Ruwei said: "I would rather fall before the sword and be a ghost of the Southern Court—how could I bear to betray my lord and be disloyal to whom I serve?"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him to see Liu Yu. Ruwei said, "I would rather fall before the sword and be a ghost of the Southern Court than betray my lord and be disloyal to whom I serve."

sentences.zh: 力拒不行，乃至京師，瀕死者數四。

translations.literal: He forcefully refused and would not go; he reached the capital only after nearing death four times.
translations.idiomatic: He forcefully refused. He reached the Jin capital only after nearly dying four times.

sentences.zh: 豫僭號，汝為持頤浩書與之，開陳禍福，勉以忠義，使歸朝廷。

translations.literal: When Yu usurped a title, Ruwei bore Yihao's letter to him, explained fortune and calamity, urged loyalty and righteousness, and sought to make him return to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu usurped a title, Ruwei bore Lü Yihao's letter to him, explained fortune and calamity, urged loyalty and righteousness, and sought to make him return to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 豫悚而立曰：「使人！

translations.literal: Yu rose in alarm and said: "Envoy!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu rose in alarm and said, "Envoy!

sentences.zh: 使人！

translations.literal: Envoy!
translations.idiomatic: Envoy!

sentences.zh: 使豫自新南歸，人誰直我，獨不見張邦昌之事乎？

translations.literal: If you make Yu renew himself and return south, who will speak for me? Have you alone not seen what happened to Zhang Bangchang?
translations.idiomatic: If you make me renew myself and return south, who will speak for me? Have you not seen what happened to Zhang Bangchang?

sentences.zh: 業已至此，夫復何言。」

translations.literal: Matters have already come to this—what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Matters have already come to this—what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 即拘留汝為。

translations.literal: He thereupon detained Ruwei.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon detained Ruwei.

sentences.zh: 然以汝為儒士，乃授通直郎、同知曹州以誘之，固辭。

translations.literal: Yet because Ruwei was a Confucian scholar, he was given Direct Gentleman and Vice Governor of Caozhou to entice him; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because Ruwei was a scholar, they offered him direct gentleman and vice governor of Caozhou to entice him; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 遂連結先陷於北者淩唐佐、李亙、李儔為腹心，以機密歸報朝廷。

translations.literal: He then joined with Ling Tangzuo, Li Geng, and Li Chou, who had earlier fallen into the north, as his inner circle, and reported secrets back to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined with Ling Tangzuo, Li Geng, and Li Chou, who had earlier been trapped in the north, as his inner circle and reported secrets back to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 唐佐等所遣僧及卒為邏者所獲，汝為所遣王現、邵邦光善達，朝廷皆官之。

translations.literal: Monks and soldiers sent by Tangzuo and others were captured by patrols; Wang Xian and Shao Bangguang sent by Ruwei reached the court successfully, and the court gave them all offices.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and soldiers sent by Tangzuo and others were captured by patrols. Wang Xian and Shao Bangguang sent by Ruwei reached the court successfully, and the court gave them offices.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年，汝為亡歸，作《恢復方略》獻於朝，且曰：「今和好雖定，計必背盟，不可遽馳。」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, Ruwei escaped and returned, composed "Strategy for Restoration" and presented it to the court, and said: "Though peace is now settled, they are sure to break the treaty—you must not rush to act."
translations.idiomatic: In 1143, Ruwei escaped and returned, composed Strategy for Restoration and presented it to the court, and said, "Though peace is now settled, they are sure to break the treaty—you must not rush to act."

sentences.zh: 時秦檜當國，置不復問。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui held the state and set it aside without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Hui held power and ignored it.

sentences.zh: 獨禮部尚書蘇符憐之，為言於朝，換宣教郎，添差通判處州。

translations.literal: Only Minister of Rites Su Fu pitied him, spoke for him at court, and he was changed to Instruction Gentleman with additional assignment as Vice Governor of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only Minister of Rites Su Fu pitied him and spoke for him at court. He was made instruction gentleman with additional assignment as vice governor of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗憶其忠，特轉通直郎。

translations.literal: Gaozong remembered his loyalty and specially transferred him to Direct Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong remembered his loyalty and specially promoted him to direct gentleman.

sentences.zh: 汝為遂上丞相書，言：「用兵之道，取勝在於得勢，成功在乎投機。

translations.literal: Ruwei then submitted a letter to the chief councilor, saying: "In the way of using troops, victory lies in gaining momentum; success depends on seizing opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Ruwei then wrote to the chief councilor, saying, "In warfare, victory lies in gaining momentum; success depends on seizing opportunity.

sentences.zh: 女真乘襲取契丹之銳，梟視狼顧，以窺中原，一旦長驅直搗京闕，升平既久，人不知兵，故彼得投其機而速發，由是猖獗兩河，以成盜據之功。

translations.literal: The Jurchen rode the sharp edge of seizing the Khitan, looked about like owls and wolves eyeing the Central Plains; in one day they drove straight to the capital gates. Peace had lasted long and people knew nothing of war; thus they could seize their opportunity and strike swiftly, and thereby ran rampant through the two He regions to accomplish their feat of bandit seizure.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen rode the momentum of defeating the Khitan, eyed the Central Plains like wolves, and in one thrust drove straight to the capital. Peace had lasted so long that people knew nothing of war; they seized their opportunity and struck swiftly, running rampant through the two He regions to establish their hold.

sentences.zh: 既而關右、河朔豪傑士民避地轉鬥，從歸聖朝，將士戮力，削平群盜，破逐英雄，百戰之餘，勇氣萬倍。

translations.literal: Then heroes and people of Guan west and Hebei north fled and fought their way, returning to the holy court; officers and soldiers joined their strength, cut down bandit hordes, defeated and drove off heroes; after a hundred battles their courage was ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: Then heroes and people of the northwest and Hebei fled and fought their way back to the Song court. Officers and soldiers joined their strength, crushed bandits, and defeated enemy champions. After a hundred battles their courage was ten thousandfold.

sentences.zh: 回思曩昔，痛自慚悔，人人扼腕切齒，願當一戰。

translations.literal: Looking back on the past, each painfully repents in shame; every man clenches his wrist and grinds his teeth, wishing to fight one decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on the past, each man repents in shame, clenches his fist, grinds his teeth, and longs for one decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 加以金人兵老氣衰，思歸益切，是以去歲順昌孤壘，力挫其鋒。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jin troops are aged and their spirit decayed, their longing to return ever keener—thus last year at the lone fortress of Shunchang their edge was forcefully blunted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Jin troops are aged and weary, their longing to return ever keener—thus last year at the lone fortress of Shunchang their advance was forcefully blunted.

sentences.zh: 方其狼狽逃遁之際，此國家乘勝進戰之時也。

translations.literal: Just as they fled in disarray, this was the time for the state to ride victory and advance to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they fled in disarray, this was the time for the state to press its advantage.

sentences.zh: 惜乎王師遽旋，撫其機而不發，遂未能殄滅醜類，以成恢復之功。

translations.literal: Alas, the imperial army swiftly turned back, stroked the opportunity but did not release it, and thus could not exterminate the vile host to accomplish the merit of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the imperial army swiftly withdrew, stroked the opportunity but did not seize it, and thus could not destroy the enemy to accomplish restoration.

sentences.zh: 今聞其力圖大舉，轉輸淮北，其設意豈小哉！

translations.literal: Now I hear they are striving for a great campaign and transporting supplies north of the Huai—their intent is surely no small matter!
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear they are planning a major campaign and transporting supplies north of the Huai—their intent is surely no small matter!

sentences.zh: 所慮秋冬復肆猖獗，兀朮不死，兵革不休，雖欲各保邊陲，安可得也？

translations.literal: What is feared is that in autumn and winter they will again run rampant; while Wuzhu is not dead, arms will not cease—though each wishes to secure only the borderlands, how can that be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in autumn and winter they will run rampant again. While Wuzhu lives, war will not cease—though each wishes only to secure the borders, how can that be achieved?

sentences.zh: 今當乘去歲淮上破賊之勢，特降哀痛之詔，聲言親征，約諸帥長驅直搗，某月日各到東京，協謀並力，以俘馘兀術為急。」

translations.literal: Now we should ride the momentum of last year's defeat of the enemy on the Huai, specially issue a grief-stricken edict, proclaim a personal campaign, appoint the various commanders to drive straight forward, each to reach Dongjing on a set month and day, join plans and combine strength, and make capturing Wuzhu the urgent task."
translations.idiomatic: Now we should ride the momentum of last year's victory on the Huai, issue a grief-stricken edict proclaiming a personal campaign, appoint the commanders to advance straight forward, each to reach Dongjing on a set date, join plans and combine strength, and make capturing Wuzhu the urgent task."

sentences.zh: 又言：「兀朮好勇妄作，再起兵端，所共謀者，叛亡群盜而已。

translations.literal: He also said: "Wuzhu loves courage and acts recklessly; he raises arms again—the only ones he plots with are renegade and fugitive bandit hordes.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Wuzhu loves courage and acts recklessly. He raises arms again—the only ones he plots with are renegade bandits.

sentences.zh: 去夏諸帥各舉，金人奔命敗北之不暇，兀朮深以為慮，故為先發制人之動，所恃者不過自能聚兵合勢，料王師以諸帥分軍爾。

translations.literal: Last summer the various commanders each advanced; the Jin had no leisure beyond fleeing for their lives in defeat northward; Wuzhu was deeply troubled, and therefore made a move to strike first and control others; what he relies on is only that he himself can gather troops and combine strength, calculating that the imperial army will divide forces among the various commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Last summer the commanders each advanced and the Jin fled north in defeat. Wuzhu was deeply troubled and therefore struck first. He relies only on gathering troops and combining strength, calculating that the imperial army will divide forces among the commanders.

sentences.zh: 今計其步騎不過十萬，王師雲集，其眾數倍，合勢刻期，並進戮力，何憂乎不勝？

translations.literal: Now I estimate their infantry and cavalry do not exceed one hundred thousand; the imperial army gathers like clouds, several times their number; combine momentum, fix a date, advance together with joined strength—why worry about not winning?
translations.idiomatic: I estimate their infantry and cavalry do not exceed one hundred thousand. The imperial army gathers in far greater numbers. Combine forces, fix a date, advance together—why worry about not winning?

sentences.zh: 若以諸帥難相統屬，宜除川、陝一路，專當撒離喝，權合諸帥為兩節制，公選大臣任觀軍容為宣慰之職，往來調和諸帥，使之上下同心，左右戮力，則勢既合不為賊所料矣。

translations.literal: If the various commanders are hard to place under unified command, the Sichuan-Shaanxi circuit alone should be set aside to deal specially with Salihun; temporarily combine the commanders into two regional commands; openly select a great minister to serve as observer of military appearance in a pacification commissioner's post, going back and forth to harmonize the commanders so that above and below are of one heart and left and right join strength—then momentum will be combined and the enemy cannot calculate it.
translations.idiomatic: If the commanders are hard to unify, set aside the Sichuan-Shaanxi circuit to deal with Salihun alone; temporarily combine the commanders into two regional commands; select a great minister as military observer and pacification commissioner to harmonize the commanders so that all join in one effort—then our strength will be united and the enemy cannot anticipate us.

sentences.zh: 不然，分軍出陳、蔡，直搗東都，賊必首尾勢分，復以重兵急擊，然後以舟師自淮繇新河入鉅野澤，以步兵自洛渡懷、衛入太行山，以襲其內。

translations.literal: Otherwise, divide the army out from Chen and Cai, strike straight at the eastern capital—the enemy must divide head and tail; then with heavy troops strike urgently, and afterward send the fleet from the Huai through the new river into Juye Marsh, and infantry from the Luo crossing through Huai and Wei into the Taihang Mountains to strike their interior.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, divide forces from Chen and Cai and strike straight at the eastern capital—the enemy must divide their forces. Then strike with heavy troops, send the fleet from the Huai through the new river into Juye Marsh, and send infantry from the Luo crossing through Huai and Wei into the Taihang Mountains to strike their interior.

sentences.zh: 舟師入鉅野，則齊魯搖，步兵入太行，則三晉應，賊勢雖欲合而不分，亦難乎為計矣。」

translations.literal: When the fleet enters Juye, Qi and Lu will be shaken; when infantry enter the Taihang, the three Jin regions will respond; though the enemy's power wishes to combine and not divide, it will be hard to make plans."
translations.idiomatic: When the fleet enters Juye, Qi and Lu will be shaken; when infantry enter the Taihang, the three Jin regions will respond. Though the enemy wish to keep their forces united, they will find it hard to plan."

sentences.zh: 久之，有告汝為於金人以蠟書言其機事者，大索不獲，尋知南歸。

translations.literal: After a long time someone reported to the Jin that Ruwei had used wax letters to speak of secret affairs; a great search found nothing, and soon they learned he had returned south.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time someone reported to the Jin that Ruwei had used secret wax letters to report confidential affairs. A great search found nothing, and soon they learned he had returned south.

sentences.zh: 檜將械送金人，汝為變姓名為趙復，徒步入蜀。

translations.literal: Hui was about to send him in fetters to the Jin; Ruwei changed his name to Zhao Fu and entered Shu on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was about to send him in fetters to the Jin. Ruwei changed his name to Zhao Fu and walked into Shu.

sentences.zh: 汝為身長七尺，疏眉秀目，望之如神仙。

translations.literal: Ruwei was seven chi tall, with sparse brows and elegant eyes; seen from afar he seemed an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Ruwei stood seven chi tall, with sparse brows and elegant eyes; seen from afar he seemed an immortal.

sentences.zh: 楊企道者，遇之溪上，企道曰：「必奇士也。」

translations.literal: Yang Qidao met him by a stream and said: "He must be an extraordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qidao met him by a stream and said, "He must be an extraordinary man."

sentences.zh: 款留之，見其議論英發，洞貫古今，靖康間離亂事歷言之，企道益驚，遂定交，假僧舍居之。

translations.literal: He detained him warmly, saw his discourse brilliant and penetrating, thoroughly versed in past and present; he narrated in detail the disorders of the Jingkang era; Qidao was ever more astonished, and they formed a bond, lodging him in a borrowed monks' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He detained him warmly. His discourse was brilliant and penetrating, thoroughly versed in past and present. He narrated in detail the disorders of the Jingkang era. Qidao was ever more astonished, and they became friends, lodging him in a borrowed monks' quarters.

sentences.zh: 檜死，汝為曰：「朝廷除此巨蠹，中原恢復有日矣。」

translations.literal: When Hui died, Ruwei said: "The court has removed this great pest—the Central Plains will be restored in due time."
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui died, Ruwei said, "The court has removed this great pest—the Central Plains will be restored before long."

sentences.zh: 企道勸其理前事，汝為慨然太息曰：「吾結髮讀書，奮身一出，志在為國復仇，收還土宇，頗為諸公所知，命繆數奇，軋於權臣，今老矣，新進貴人，無知我者。」

translations.literal: Qidao urged him to take up former affairs; Ruwei sighed deeply and said: "From youth I tied my hair and read books, threw myself forth once, my aim to avenge the state and recover territory—many lords knew me somewhat; fate was perverse and my lot strange, I was crushed by powerful ministers; now I am old, and the newly risen nobles know me not."
translations.idiomatic: Qidao urged him to take up former affairs. Ruwei sighed deeply and said, "From youth I studied and threw myself into service, aiming to avenge the state and recover our territory. Many lords once knew me, but fate was perverse and I was crushed by powerful ministers. Now I am old, and the newly risen nobles do not know me."

sentences.zh: 汝為能知死期，嘗祭其先，終日大慟，將終，神氣不亂。

translations.literal: Ruwei could know the time of his death; he once sacrificed to his ancestors and wailed greatly all day; nearing the end, his spirit and bearing were not disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Ruwei knew the time of his death. He once sacrificed to his ancestors and wailed all day. Near the end, his spirit remained composed.

sentences.zh: 汝為俶儻尚氣節，博物洽聞，飲酒至斗餘，未嘗見其醉，或歌或哭，涕淚俱下。

translations.literal: Ruwei was free-spirited and valued integrity; broadly learned and well informed; he drank more than a dou at a time yet was never seen drunk; sometimes he sang or wept, tears and mucus flowing together.
translations.idiomatic: Ruwei was free-spirited and valued integrity, broadly learned and well informed. He could drink more than a dou at a sitting yet was never seen drunk. Sometimes he sang or wept with tears streaming down.

sentences.zh: 其客蜀也，史載之、邵博、宇文亮、臣李燾相得甚歡，趙沂、王京魯、關民先、楊寀、惠疇經紀其喪事。

translations.literal: While he sojourned in Shu, Shi Zaizhi, Shao Bo, Yuwen Liang, and Li Tao were very pleased with one another; Zhao Yi, Wang Jinglu, Guan Minxian, Yang Cai, and Hui Chou managed his funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While he sojourned in Shu, he was very close to Shi Zaizhi, Shao Bo, Yuwen Liang, and Li Tao. Zhao Yi, Wang Jinglu, Guan Minxian, Yang Cai, and Hui Chou managed his funeral.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，其妻錢莫知汝為死，詣登聞鼓院以狀進，詔索之不得。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year his wife Qian did not know Ruwei had died and went to the Petition Drum Court to submit a statement; an edict sought him but he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year his wife Qian did not know Ruwei had died and went to the Petition Drum Court to submit a statement. An edict sought him but he could not be found.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年，其子南強以汝為之死哀訴於朝，參知政事虞允文，錢端禮以聞，特官一子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing his son Nanqiang mournfully appealed to the court concerning Ruwei's death; Participating in Governance Yu Yunwen and Qian Duanli reported it, and one son was specially given an office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1164 his son Nanqiang mournfully appealed to the court concerning Ruwei's death. Participating in governance Yu Yunwen and Qian Duanli reported it, and one son was specially given an office.

sentences.zh: 有《忠嘉集》行世。

translations.literal: His "Collected Works of Loyalty and Excellence" circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Works of Loyalty and Excellence circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高宗播遷，復有苗、劉之變，此何時也，鄭𣪝、王庭秀正色立朝，以爭君臣之義，顧不韙哉！

translations.literal: The commentary says: Gaozong was driven wandering, and there was again the Miao and Liu upheaval—what a time! Zheng Jue and Wang Tingxiu stood in court with stern countenance to contend for the righteousness of ruler and minister—how fearless!
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Gaozong was driven from the capital, and there came the Miao and Liu upheaval—what a time! Zheng Jue and Wang Tingxiu stood in court with stern countenance to fight for the righteousness of ruler and minister—how fearless!

sentences.zh: 仇悆愷悌君子，遺澤在民。

translations.literal: Chou Yu was a gentle and harmonious gentleman; his lingering grace remains among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Yu was a gentle and harmonious gentleman whose lingering grace remains among the people.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰「王臣蹇蹇」，高登有焉。

translations.literal: The Changes says, "The king's minister faces hardship upon hardship"—Gao Deng had this.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The king's minister faces hardship upon hardship"—Gao Deng embodied this.

sentences.zh: 婁寅亮請立太祖後為太子，能言人臣之所難言，而高宗亦慨然從之，君仁而臣直乎！

translations.literal: Lou Yinliang requested establishing a Taizu descendant as heir—he could speak what ministers find hard to speak, and Gaozong also followed with emotion—was this not a benevolent lord and upright ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Lou Yinliang requested establishing a descendant of Taizu as heir—he spoke what ministers find hard to say, and Gaozong followed with emotion—a benevolent lord and upright ministers indeed!

sentences.zh: 宋汝為歸自金國，論事切直，與寅亮俱迕秦檜，一則誣以罪譴，一則逃遁以死，於乎悕矣！

translations.literal: Song Ruwei returned from the Jin state; his discussion of affairs was cutting and direct; he and Yinliang both opposed Qin Hui—one was falsely charged and punished, the other fled and died—alas, how rare!
translations.idiomatic: Song Ruwei returned from the Jin; his counsel was cutting and direct. He and Yinliang both opposed Qin Hui—one was falsely charged and punished, the other fled and died—alas, how rare!
